    Repeated labels in category algebras #

    For Lemma 4.7 (lem:homogeneous-projection, scalar-normalization.tex): "Enlarge it to the category B' on the same labels with B'(i,j) = B(x_i,x_j). Repeated labels give matrix multiplicities, and the distinct labels give an idempotent corner of B. Thus B' is representation-finite by Morita equivalence and Lemma 3.1(1)."

    For a family F : ι → C and a relabelling σ : κ → ι, both Alg F and Alg (F ∘ σ) are idempotent corners of the category algebra of the family F ⊔ (F ∘ σ) on ι ⊕ κ, and the first corner is at a full idempotent. So if Alg F is representation-finite, so are the big algebra (Morita, isRepresentationFinite_of_full) and its corner Alg (F ∘ σ) (Lemma 3.1(1)) (isRepresentationFinite_comp). Algebras are taken opposite, so that right modules are the modules Rep F X of CategoryAlgebra.lean.
